source_text: Μωϋσῆς μὲν οὖν, πρῶτος τῶν προφητῶν γενόμενος, εἶπεν αὐτολεξεὶ οὕτως· „Οὐκ ἐκλείψει ἄρχων ἐξ Ἰούδα οὐδὲ ἡγούμενος ἐκ τῶν μηρῶν αὐτοῦ, ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ᾧ ἀπόκειται· καὶ αὐτὸς ἔσται προσδοκία ἐθνῶν, δεσμεύων πρὸς ἄμπελον τὸν πῶλον αὐτοῦ, πλύνων ἐν αἵματι σταφυλῆς τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ“. Ὑμέτερον οὖν ἐστιν ἀκριβῶς ἐξετάσαι καὶ μαθεῖν, μέχρι τίνος ἥν ἄρχων καὶ βασιλεὺς ἐν Ἰουδαίοις ἴδιος αὐτῶν· μέχρι τῆς φανερώσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ ἡμετέρου διδασκάλου καὶ τῶν ἀγνοουμένων προφητειῶν ἐξηγητοῦ, ὡς προεῤῥέθη ὑπὸ τοῦ θείου ἁγίου προφητικοῦ πνεύματος διὰ τοῦ Μωϋσέως μὴ ἐκλείψειν ἄρχοντα ἀπὸ Ἰουδαίων, ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ᾧ ἀπόκειται τὸ βασίλειον. Ἰούδας γὰρ προπάτωρ Ἰουδαίων, ἀφ᾿ οὗ καὶ τὸ Ἰουδαῖοι καλεῖσθαι ἐσχήκασι· καὶ ὑμεῖς μετὰ τὴν γενομένην αὐτοῦ φανέρωσιν καὶ Ἰουδαίων ἐβαλισεύσατε καὶ τῆς ἐκείνων πάσης γῆς ἐκρατήσατε. Τὸ δὲ „Αὐτὸς ἔσται προσδοκία ἐθνῶν“ μηνυτικὸν ἦν, ὅτι ἐκ πάντων τῶν ἐθνῶν προσδοκήσουσιν αὐτὸν πάλιν παραγενησόμενον, ὅπερ ὄψει ὑμῖν πάρεστιν ἰδεῖν καὶ ἔργῳ πεισθῆναι· ἐκ πάντων γὰρ γενῶν ἀνθρώπων προσδοκῶσι τὸν ἐν Ἰουδαίᾳ σταυρωθέντα, μεθ᾿ ὃν εὐθὺς δοριάλωτος ὑμῖν ἡ γῆ Ἰουδαίων παρεδόθη. Τὸ δὲ „Δεσμεύων πρὸς ἄμπελον τὸν πῶλον αὐτοῦ καὶ πλύνων τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ ἐν αἵματι σταφυλῆς“ σύμβολον δηλωτικὸν ἦν τῶν γενησομένων τῷ Χριστῷ καὶ τῶν ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ πραχθησομένων. Πῶλος γάρ τις ὄνου εἱστήκει ἔν τινι εἰσόδῳ κώμης πρὸς ἄμπελον δεδεμένος, ὃν ἐκέλευσεν ἀγαγεῖν αὐτῷ τότε τοὺς γνωρίμους αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀχθέντος ἐπιβὰς ἐκάθισε καὶ εἰσελήλυθεν εἰς τὰ Ἱεροσόλυμα, ἔνθα τὸ μέγιστον ἱερὸν ἦν Ἰουδαίων, ὃ ὑφ᾿ ὑμῶν ὕστερον κατεστράφη· καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐσταυρώθη, ὅπως τὸ λεῖπον τῆς προφητείας συντελεσθῇ. Τὸ γὰρ „Πλύνων τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ ἔν αἵματι σταφυλῆς“ προαγγελτικὸν ἦν τοῦ πάθους, οὗ πάσχειν ἔμελλε δι᾿ αἵματος καθαίρων τοὺς πιστεύοντας αὐτῷ. Ἡ γὰρ κεκλημένη ὑπὸ τοῦ θείου πνεύματος διὰ τοῦ προφήτου στολὴ οἱ πιστεύοντες αὐτῷ εἰσιν ἄνθρωποι, ἐν οἷς οἰκεῖ τὸ παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ σπέρμα, ὁ λόγος. Τὸ δὲ εἰρημένον αἷμα τῆς σταφυλῆς σημναντικὸν τοῦ ἔχειν μὲν αἷμα τὸν φανησόμενον, ἀλλ᾿ οὐκ ἐξ ἀνθρωπείου σπέρματος ἀλλ᾿ ἐκ θείας δυνάμεως. Ἡ δὲ πρώτη δύναμις μετὰ τὸν πατέρα πάντων καὶ δεσπότην θεὸν καὶ υἱὸς ὁ λόγος ἐστίν· ὃς τίνα τρόπον σαρκοποιηθεὶς ἄνθρωπος γέγονεν, ἐν τοῖς ἑξῆς ἐροῦμεν. Ὃν τρόπον γὰρ τὸ τῆς ἀμπέλου αἷμα οὐκ ἄνθρωπος πεποίηκεν ἀλλ᾿ ὁ θεός, οὕτως καὶ τοῦτο ἐμηνύετο οὐκ ἐξ ἀνθρωπείου σπέρματος γενήσεσθαι τὸ αἷμα ἀλλ᾿ ἐκ δυνάμεως θεοῦ, ὡς προέφημεν. Καὶ Ἡσαΐας δέ, ἄλλος προφήτης, τὰ αὐτὰ δι᾿ ἄλλων ῥήσεων προφητεύων οὕτως εἶπεν· „Ἀνατελεῖ ἄστρον ἐξ Ἰακώβ, καὶ ἄνθος ἀναβήσεται ἀπὸ τῆς ῥίζης Ἰεσσαί· καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν βραχίονα αὐτοῦ ἔθνη ἐλπιοῦσιν“. Ἄστρον δὲ φωτεινὸν ἀνέτειλε, καὶ ἄνθος ἀνέβη ἀπὸ τῆς ῥίζης Ἰεσσαί, οὗτος ὁ Χριστός. Διὰ γὰρ παρθένου τῆς ἀπὸ τοῦ σπέρματος Ἰακώβ, τοῦ γενομένου πατρὸς Ἰούδα, τοῦ δεδηλωμένου Ἰουδαίων πατρός, διὰ δυνάμεως θεοῦ ἀπεκυήθη· καὶ Ἰεσσαὶ προπάτωρ μὲν κατὰ τὸ λόγιον γεγένηται, τοῦ δὲ Ἰακὼβ καὶ τοῦ Ἰούδα κατὰ γένους διαδοχὴν υἱὸς ὑπῆρχεν.
pass_a_gloss: Moses, therefore, having become the first of the prophets, spoke in these very words: 'A ruler will not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until what is reserved comes; and he will be the expectation of nations, binding his colt to a vine, and washing his robe in the blood of a grape.' It is yours, then, to examine carefully and learn until which time they had a ruler and king of their own among the Jews; until the appearance of Jesus Christ, our teacher and interpreter of the unknown prophecies, as was foretold by the divine Holy Spirit through Moses, that a ruler would not fail from the Jews until what is reserved comes. For Judah was the forefather of the Jews, from whom the Jews also got their name; and you, after his appearance, ruled the Jews and took possession of all their land. The phrase 'He will be the expectation of nations' was a sign that all nations will expect him when he comes again, which you have the opportunity to see and be convinced by deed; for people from all nations expect the one crucified in Judah, after whom the land of the Jews was immediately handed over to you as a gift. The phrase 'Binding his colt to a vine and washing his robe in the blood of a grape' was a symbolic declaration of what would happen to Christ and what would be done by him. A certain colt of a donkey was standing tied to a vine in the entrance of a village, which his acquaintances were ordered to bring to him at that time, and when it was brought, he mounted it and sat on it and entered Jerusalem, where the greatest temple of the Jews was, which was later destroyed by you; and after these things, he was crucified, so that the remainder of the prophecy might be fulfilled. For the phrase 'Washing his robe in the blood of a grape' was a foretelling of the passion he would suffer, cleansing those who believe in him through blood. The robe, which was spoken of by the divine Spirit through the prophet, are the people who believe in him, in whom the seed from God, the Word, dwells. The blood of the grape that was mentioned is a sign that the one who appeared has blood, but not from human seed, but from divine power. The first power after the Father of all and Lord God is the Word, the Son; who, having become flesh, became a man, which we will discuss later. For just as the blood of the grape was not made by a person, but by God, so also this was indicated, that the blood would not be born from human seed, but from the power of God, as we foretold. And Isaiah, another prophet, prophesying the same things through different expressions, spoke thus: 'A star will rise from Jacob, and a flower will bloom from the root of Jesse; and nations will hope in his arm.' A bright star has risen, and a flower has bloomed from the root of Jesse, this being Christ. For through a virgin from the seed of Jacob, who became the father of Judah, who was declared the father of the Jews, he was born through the power of God; and Jesse was a forefather according to the word, and a son existed in the succession of Jacob and Judah by birth.
pass_b_english: Moses, the first of the prophets, spoke these exact words: "A ruler will not cease from Judah, nor a leader from his line, until the one to whom it is reserved arrives; and he will be the expectation of the nations, tethering his colt to a vine and washing his robe in the blood of the grape" (Genesis 49:10). It is your task to examine carefully and learn until what time the Jews had a ruler and king of their own; that time lasted until the appearance of Jesus Christ, our teacher and the interpreter of the obscure prophecies, just as the divine Holy Spirit foretold through Moses that a ruler would not cease from the Jews until the one to whom the kingdom is reserved should come. For Judah was the forefather of the Jews, and from him they received the very name 'Jews'; and after his manifestation you ruled the Jews and seized possession of all their land. The statement "He will be the expectation of the nations" was a sign that all nations would await his return, and you now have the opportunity to witness this and be convinced by the fact itself; for people from every nation expect the one who was crucified in Judea, after whose death the land of the Jews was immediately handed over to you as a conquered territory.

The phrase "Tethering his colt to a vine and washing his robe in the blood of the grape" was a symbolic declaration of what would happen to Christ and what he would accomplish. A certain donkey's colt stood tied to a vine at a village entrance; he ordered his acquaintances to bring it to him, and when it was brought he mounted it, sat upon it, and entered Jerusalem, where the great temple of the Jews stood, which you later destroyed; and after these things he was crucified, so that the rest of the prophecy might be fulfilled. For the words "Washing his robe in the blood of the grape" foretold the passion he would endure, cleansing those who believe in him through his blood. The robe, spoken of by the divine Spirit through the prophet, represents the people who believe in him, in whom the seed from God, the Word, dwells. The mentioned blood of the grape signifies that the one who appeared possesses blood, yet not from human seed but from divine power. The first power after the Father of all and Lord God is the Word, the Son; who, having become flesh, became a man — a matter we will discuss later. For just as the blood of the grape is not produced by a human but by God, so it was indicated that his blood would not come from human seed but from the power of God, as we foretold.

And Isaiah, another prophet, prophesying the same things through different words, declared: "A star will rise from Jacob, and a shoot will spring from the root of Jesse; and the nations will hope in his arm" (Isaiah 11:1). A bright star has risen, and a flower has bloomed from the root of Jesse — this is the Christ. For through a virgin descended from the seed of Jacob, who became the father of Judah, who was designated the father of the Jews, he was born by the power of God; and Jesse became a forefather according to the oracle, while also standing as a son in the line of descent from Jacob and Judah.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the distinction between the blood of the grape and the divine nature of Christ's blood. Scripture citations (Genesis 49:10 and Isaiah 11:1) are correctly identified and applied to the quoted prophetic passages. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek source.
